en.title: Identify Names Registered Repeatedly Using Anagrams
en.description:
No two real names are anagrams of each other, and every registered name is an anagram of some real name. Find the real names registered more than 1 time and output them in lexicographic order; if there are none, output None. Repeated identical registered names each count as a separate account.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n m, followed by n lines of real names and m lines of registered names. 1≤n,m≤100000; each name has length 1..10 and contains only lowercase letters; real names are distinct and no two are anagrams of each other.
en.output: Output on one line, in lexicographic order, the real names that were registered repeatedly, separated by spaces; if there are none, output None.
en.explanation: The answers are henry; jerry tom; None.
hints: Use a name's sorted characters as its signature, count how often each registered signature occurs, then keep the real names whose frequency is greater than 1 and sort them.
